image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) swimming in blue water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a chestnut breast, and a greyish-brown body. One orange webbed foot is visible paddling underwater. The bill is bright yellow.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow, matching the description for a mallard drake.
The eye is visible on the side of the head and appears dark/black.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a swimming duck, appearing streamlined and floating correctly on the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plumage matches the specific Mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey/brown flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is visible underwater. It shows the correct anatomical position (set back) and structure (webbed foot).
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing typical feather layering and shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, short and slightly upturned, consistent with a drake.
